newsitem.title: UK: UK financial overseas earnings at record levels.
newsitem.headline: UK financial overseas earnings at record levels.

text.p: The net overseas earnings of the UK financial sector reached a record 22.7 billion stg in 1996, 2.0 billion higher than the previous year, British Invisibles said on Thursday.
"This was another record year for the financial sector," said Duncan McKenzie, British Invisibles' economic advisor said.

"Further growth in its overseas earnings reflects the consolidation and strengthening of London's leading position in many financial markets. Financial services are increasingly important to both the UK and world economy -- and the UK is well positioned to build on its present strengths," he said.

The current account has benefited greatly from the financial sector's contribution, with the invisible earnings surplus leaping by 4.3 billion stg, taking it to 12.2 billion. The UK posted a current account deficit of just 435 million stg in 1996.

British Invisibles said earnings from the service sector rose 162 million stg to 12.8 billion and accounted for the majority of invisible earnings. Investment income rose by 1.8 billion stg to 9.8 billion.
Banks' net earnings rose to 7.1 billion stg, from 5.9 billion, regaining the ground lost in 1995.

This recovery was mainly due to a much reduced net outflow on direct investment income from 2.0 billion stg down to 1.1 billion. A rise of 327 million stg to 1.5 billion in portfolio investment income also contributed to the buoyant picture for banks.

But the picture for the insurance sector was less encouraging with a drop in overseas earnings to 6.1 billion stg after a rise in 1995 of 2.9 billion which took the total to 6.9 billion. But the 1996 total was still higher than any year prior to 1995.
Companies' earnings rose by 426 million stg to 4.7 billion as an increase in their portfolio investment income more than offset a reduction in underwriting and direct investment income.
Overseas earnings for Lloyd's fell by 1.6 billion stg to 508 million, affected both by recovery in profits attributable to overseas members and also the establishment of Equitas.
Securities dealers had a good year with net overseas earnings increasing by 432 million stg to 2.2 billion.

Other traders, too, gained ground and reached a new peak in earnings - those of commodity traders, bullion dealers and export houses increased by over 80 million stg to 642 million while overseas earnings of money-market brokers rose to 134 million.
In the maritime sector, earnings of the Baltic Exchange declined from 292 million to 260 million stg, while Lloyd's Register's were unchanged at 57 million.
